user_report: Power-cycled and played the file once, then stopped so the helper log could be fetched before any replay overwrote it.

power_cycle_evidence.syslog_first_line: Aug 27 07:25:17 MiSTer syslog.info syslogd started: BusyBox v1.33.1

cold_run_outcome: CLEAN - zero cadence outliers, zero missed deadlines, 449 pictures, 448 swaps, all 15,150,646 bytes accepted, error_flags 0
cold_determinism: cold is not deterministic: of four verified cold runs, three gapped (entry 568, block 1 run 1, block 3 run 1) and one was clean (this entry)

arm_helper_log.would_block_placement: every logged would_block in both the cold and the warm log carries submitted=0 and precedes the first byte; after read event 1 neither log records another
arm_helper_log.conclusion: EAGAIN never occurs during steady delivery in either thermal state, so the four-chunk per-poll budget is binding in both. The cold penalty is concentrated entirely before the first byte, where cold shows 3.5 times as many would-block polls as warm.

dead_time_analysis.method: for each deadline record, compare the measured time to the deadline against the time the same accepted-byte count requires at the warm steady rate of 1,392,000 B/s; the residual is dead time before delivery effectively began
dead_time_analysis.rate_derivation: 4 chunks x 4096 bytes per poll at the implied 85 Hz poll rate; independently validated by the warm residuals below
dead_time_analysis.interpretation: the steady delivery rate is identical cold and warm; five independent warm sessions are predicted within plus or minus 1.2 ms. What varies is dead time before the first byte, which is zero warm and reaches 63.8 ms cold, and it tracks severity: 63.8 ms produced two missed deadlines, 27.8 and 13.9 ms produced one each.

correction_to_entry_571.superseded_claim: entry 571 states that on a cold start the upstream feed runs at 0.94 times realtime and below the rate the stream requires
correction_to_entry_571.correction: the feed does not run slow. Steady delivery is 1,392,000 B/s in every measured state. The apparent 0.94 figure divided accepted bytes by elapsed time and thereby folded the pre-first-byte startup stall into an apparent rate. The defect is a late start, not a slow feed.
correction_to_entry_571.consequence: raising the per-poll chunk count or buffer size in mediaplayer_poll() would not correct the defect, because steady throughput was never the limiting quantity

fix_implications.ruled_out: raising the four-chunk per-poll budget; steady rate is not the constraint
fix_implications.candidate_a: reduce cold first-byte latency on the helper side, for example by priming or reading ahead in the media source before the download is asserted
fix_implications.candidate_b: absorb the dead time before the first cadence slot in the startup controller; the 64-KiB clean video queue holds 64.9 ms of stream at nominal rate, which only just covers the worst observed 63.8 ms dead time
fix_implications.note: candidate B returns the boundary to the startup controller that entries 569 and 571 had ruled out, but now with a quantified requirement rather than a byte threshold

scope_limitations: The cold run captured here was clean and therefore contributes no deadline record and no dead-time datapoint; its contribution is the would_block count of 670.
Cold sampling remains n=4 across all work.

The 85 Hz poll rate is inferred from throughput arithmetic, not measured in MiSTer main; the warm residuals validate the resulting rate but not the rate's decomposition into chunk count and poll frequency.

The helper log carries no timestamps, so the 670 would-block polls cannot be converted to a duration and the dead time is inferred from telemetry arithmetic rather than measured directly on the ARM side.
input_starved_cycles_since_previous_swap remains cumulative rather than contiguous.
Page-cache state is still not directly measured.
